integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Fifteen seconds of a live-action orchestral performance photographed from this EXACT audience position. The supplied image defines the physical room, every seat and background person, the pit barrier, burgundy velvet scenic surface and gold carved architecture. The camera is locked to a heavy tripod from the first frame through the last: fixed position, fixed focal length, fixed framing, focus and exposure. The orchestra performs inside the existing sunken pit, with the camera staying behind its existing red-topped front barrier. Same seated spectators at the same scale and floor positions. Normal real adult people, photographic fabric, wood, gold plaster and violin materials.

The large background consists of one continuous stationary expanse of opaque dark BURGUNDY VELVET with its existing gold edging and folds. Its closed centre seam and gold bottom border remain exactly as pictured. This massive fabric surface is a fixed physical scenic backing for the entire orchestral passage; the surface stays continuous and opaque across the full portal for every frame. It has no action in this shot. The existing steady warm-white practical lamps maintain the same natural gold/burgundy colour balance.

The moving subjects are the real seated orchestra players below that fixed velvet surface. Both prominent violinists seen from behind retain their exact faces, hair, black concert clothes, seats, instruments and music stands. Each violin rests on its owner's shoulder, the left hand supports the neck and the right hand guides that same bow. Bows remain rigid physical wooden sticks with hair contacting strings; hands, wrists and elbows remain anatomically connected.

At0-5s the violinist just left of centre completes a slow bow stroke, lifts the wrist slightly and reverses that same bow on the strings, with a small supported shoulder response. The violinist on the right continues a different sustained stroke before reversing, independently. Other musicians maintain their own seated playing movements. Foreground spectators keep their exact original postures and their hips in the same chairs, with only breathing and small natural head movements. Their hands stay at rest in their original positions, no new foreground gesture or object. Chair backs, brass posts and the pit barrier are fixed and unchanged.

At5-10s the violinists carry the next musical phrase with separate short bow changes and small elbow movements, left hands staying attached to the same violin necks. A seated player farther left takes a breath and adjusts only their shoulders, preserving seat position and instrument. The audience listens quietly. Retain the exact visible faces, body sizes, garments and physical objects throughout, distinct people with solid single outlines. The background velvet surface and room geometry remain stationary.

At10-15.08s the same players continue supported independent bowing, breathing and restrained shoulder responses through the final frame. One reverses a bow while the other finishes the preceding stroke, without exchanging instruments or mirroring entire bodies. All spectators remain seated and attentive, no clapping. The shot ends during the continuing orchestral performance, in the SAME fixed camera composition, with the full continuous opaque burgundy velvet scenic backing still completely unchanged and every person physically grounded. All action remains in the orchestra pit; nothing happens on the empty stage above it.

overall_soundscape: Use only the supplied original Pixel Remaster English-recording overture interval. Preserve its exact orchestra mix, stereo, timing, gain and duration. All people remain vocally silent. No new voice, speech, singing, applause, Foley or replacement music. Broad instrumental acting only, no claim of note-perfect fingering.

non_diegetic_music: N/A; original recorded overture is the sole score.
